text:
emma: Quick report - onboarding quickstart failing for a user using jsonMode + strict schema. Tool parameters include an optional object with defaults, but Node SDK is stripping keys equal to defaults before sending. The schema validator (on the sample handler) is configured to require the property presence even if default applies, so it errors: 'missing required property: options.retry_limit'.

josh: Wait, SDK strips fields that are equal to defaults? That's new. Which version and where is the default defined (tool schema vs server-side defaults)?

emma: In this case, tool schema: 
```json
{"name":"fetch_with_options","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"query":{"type":"string"},"options":{"type":"object","properties":{"retry_limit":{"type":"integer","default":3},"timeout_ms":{"type":"integer","default":1000}},"required":["retry_limit","timeout_ms"]},"required":["query"]}}
```
We sent arguments {"query":"foo","options":{"timeout_ms":1000}} from the quickstart. The Node SDK preflight serializer removed retry_limit because it equals the schema default (3) and tried to send a compact payload without defaults. But the sample-kit schema validator expects required keys present (even if default exists) so it rejects. Python SDK sends the explicit default when omitted by user.

priya: Hmm. That's a parity and policy mismatch. Historically SDKs preserved all declared schema properties on the wire and left defaulting to the handler. Someone must've added a 'stripDefaults' optimization in the Node serializer to reduce token size. That's problematic when consumers rely on presence.

josh: Agreed. Short-term we should update sample-kit validator to accept missing defaulted fields (i.e., apply schema defaults before validation) so onboarding doesn't break. Long-term, SDKs should pick a single behavior: either always send defaults as explicit fields, or never strip them. We need a policy decision.

emma: For quickfix I pushed a tiny sample-kit change that applies Ajv's default setting before validating (so missing defaults are injected). That unblocks the user's onboarding.

priya: I'll draft an RFC for SDK parity: propose Node and Py both preserve schema-declared defaults by default, but expose serializer.opt.stripDefaults = true for power users who want minimal payloads. Also add a compatibility lint: when a tool schema declares required keys under an object that also has defaults, warn in CLI quickstart because it leads to fragile assumptions.

josh: Can someone open a ticket with a minimal failing test? We should add unit tests in both SDKs and an e2e in sample-kit. Also add a docs blurb about default semantics in function-call parameters.

devx-bot: Issue created: DEVEX-1302 "jsonMode: node-sdk strips schema defaults from function-call arguments causing validator failures in sample-kit" (assign: @josh).

qa-bot: Suggested tests: 1) Node SDK roundtrip: user omits default -> SDK sends explicit default. 2) Node SDK with stripDefaults opt: ensure compact payload sent. 3) sample-kit e2e: simulate handler expecting required defaults and confirm validation passes when Ajv injects defaults.

emma: Thanks. Added the sample-kit patch behind an env var so we can revert if we decide SDKs should include defaults. Blocking DEVEX-1302 on the RFC + Node SDK change.

josh: I'll pick up the Node patch. Priya - can you lead the RFC and coordinate Py parity?

priya: Yep, will draft today and tag eng-ml for any validators that assume presence.

emma: Good catch. This one was a nasty onboarding footgun.
